column1: # Follow-up probes of corners the earlier sets leave open (#724): a task's children at a Signal that ends it, an omitted default's place in an archetype, comparison chains with <=, >= and =, <converges> on a method without a body, spawn in a defer, map literals whose keys join only at comparable, functions named at any and comparable, module constants of <unique> classes, and refinement overloads called with an int that is no literal. One question per probe, a -control beside each that might be refused for another reason. Each header and note give OpenVerse's verdict and output (Lean and C agreeing; a refusal's first line, without its position) and what either answer changes; epic_outcome and epic_lines: - until compiled and run by UEFN 43.12 (++Fortnite+Release-43.12-CL-60598086), single mode first (docs/research/versevm-live-conformance.md, "Running many probes"). The signal-* and spawn-in-suspends-defer probes suspend (Main()<suspends>); rational-less-than-int and the converges-abstract probes are asked of the compiler only.

# Not asked: whether GetRandomInt called in a condition that then fails advances the generator. On UEFN its results are not reproducible (no seed a program can set or read), so no line a probe prints would tell a rolled-back draw from a kept one; OpenVerse's generator is deterministic and has no counterpart to compare.

column7: note

The question as first written: the omitted field's default calls a printing function, C:int = Note("c", 3), Note <transacts>. Expected: refused by Epic (3582, as followup-3582/div-field-default-call). OpenVerse: refused, the default of field 'C' of holder calls Note, which might not complete (3582). If Epic refuses it (3582), OpenVerse agrees. If it admits it, a <transacts> function may be called in a field default, and it prints the order itself: OpenVerse (--extended-defaults) prints value b | value c | value a | done 10 20 3.

An archetype gives B then A, holder{B := Note("b", 20), A := Note("a", 10)}, and omits C, declared between A and B, whose default constructs a class whose block prints: where does the omitted default run among the given values? (Epic ran the given values in the order written, differential/cls-construction-order; a default that calls a function is refused, 3582, so the default is an archetype.) OpenVerse: ran, value b | default c | value a | done 10 20 (the given values, in the order written, take the places the given fields have in declaration order; an omitted default runs at its own place). If Epic prints the same, OpenVerse agrees. value b | value a | default c: omitted defaults run after every given value; default c | value b | value a: before them; OpenVerse would take either order. If Epic refuses it and the control too, a field default cannot construct a class whose block prints and the question needs another observable.

Control for cls-omitted-default-order and struct-omitted-default-order: does UEFN admit a field default that constructs a class whose block prints (no order asked: every field is omitted)? OpenVerse: ran, default c | done 1 2. If Epic prints the same, the order probes ask only about order. If it refuses it, their refusal says nothing about order (OpenVerse would then refuse such a default too, if the reason is a rule of data members).

= beside an ordering comparison in one chain: 1 < 2 = 2 and 2 = 2 < 1. OpenVerse: ran, equal y n (every adjacent pair: 1 < 2 and 2 = 2; 2 = 2 and 2 < 1). If Epic prints equal y n, OpenVerse agrees. equal n n would mean = after < compares the left operand of what is before it, (1 < 2) = 2 being 1 = 2, as < after > does. A refusal (3100 or 3509) would mean the forms do not mix: OpenVerse would refuse them.

Three comparison chains with <= and >=, in the style of differential/prec-compare-chain-mixed (Epic: a chain in one direction checks every adjacent pair; < or <= after > or >= compares the left operand of what is before it): 4 >= 4 < 5, 1 <= 1 <= 2 < 3, 5 >= 1 <= 3. OpenVerse: ran, ordered y y n (5 >= 1 <= 3 is 5 <= 3). If Epic prints ordered y y n, OpenVerse agrees. ordered y y y would mean >= then <= checks the adjacent pair (1 <= 3), unlike > then <: OpenVerse would follow.

A <computes> function that returns a module constant of a class<unique><allocates>: is the constant admitted (the class's construction effect written as <allocates>, not the default <transacts>), and may a <computes> function read it? OpenVerse: refused, the constant Shared would hold an object with var fields or of a <unique> class, which would be a new one at each use: make it a function (before any question of the function's effect). If Epic refuses it, the diagnostic says which: the constant (3512: an <allocates> construction is no data member's) or the function (reading it is not <computes>). If it admits it and prints id 7 call same, OpenVerse would admit both.

The same with the object inside an array, All:[]token = array{token{Id := 7}}. OpenVerse: refused, the constant All would hold an object with var fields or of a <unique> class, which would be a new one at each use: make it a function. If Epic refuses it, OpenVerse agrees on the verdict. If it admits it and prints id 7 uses same call same, the object in the array is made once: OpenVerse would admit it so.

The same with the object inside an option, Maybe:?token = option{token{Id := 7}}. OpenVerse: refused, the constant Maybe would hold an object with var fields or of a <unique> class, which would be a new one at each use: make it a function. If Epic refuses it, OpenVerse agrees on the verdict. If it admits it and prints id 7 uses same call same, the object in the option is made once: OpenVerse would admit it so.

A module constant of a <unique> class that has a field, Shared:token = token{Id := 7}: admitted, and is it the same object at every use (two uses compared with =, and one returned by a function)? (Epic refused a module constant of a class without specifiers, 3512, followup-3582/div-const-constructor, and admitted one of a <computes> class.) OpenVerse: refused, the constant Shared would hold an object with var fields or of a <unique> class, which would be a new one at each use: make it a function. If Epic refuses it (3512), OpenVerse agrees on the verdict. If it admits it and prints id 7 uses same call same, a module constant is one object made once: OpenVerse would admit it and make it once. different anywhere would mean the constant is made anew at a use.

A method without a body declared <converges> in an <abstract> class, overridden by a <computes> method with a body. (Epic: 3565, "The 'converges' effect is only allowed on native functions", followup-3582/div-const-converges, a function with a body.) OpenVerse: refused, shape.Sides is <converges>, so Sides cannot override it with a body: only a native function or a method without a body may be <converges> (3565), and an override has no effect the method it overrides lacks. If Epic refuses it, at the declaration (3565) or at the override, OpenVerse agrees on the verdict. If it admits it and prints sides 4, a <computes> body may override a <converges> declaration: OpenVerse would admit it.

Control for the two converges-abstract probes: the same classes with <computes> for <converges>, overridden by a <computes> method. OpenVerse: ran, sides 4. If Epic prints sides 4, a refusal of the other two is about <converges>. If it refuses this, their refusals say nothing about <converges>.

The same overridden by a method with no effect specifier. OpenVerse: refused, the same message as converges-abstract-computes-override. If Epic refuses it, OpenVerse agrees on the verdict; which error (3565 at the declaration, or an effect mismatch at the override) says whether a bodyless <converges> method is admitted at all. If it admits it and prints sides 4, OpenVerse would admit it.

map{0 => "a", "0" => "b"} with no type written: admitted (keys joined to comparable), and what do lookups by 0 and by "0" find? OpenVerse: refused, expected int, found string (at the second key). If Epic refuses it, OpenVerse agrees on the verdict. If it admits it and prints length 2 int a string b, a map literal's keys of two types join to comparable and an int and a string are different keys: OpenVerse would do so.

A map literal whose keys are of two <unique> classes, cat and dog, whose only common class, animal, is not <unique> (so not comparable): admitted, keyed by comparable? OpenVerse: refused, expected cat, found dog (the class above both is no key type, and OpenVerse does not go on to comparable). If Epic refuses it, OpenVerse agrees on the verdict. If it admits it and prints length 2 cat 1 dog 2, the keys join to comparable past a class that is not: OpenVerse would do so.

Control for map-unique-sibling-keys: the same with animal <unique>, so the keys join to a comparable class. OpenVerse: ran, length 2 cat 1 dog 2. If Epic prints the same, a refusal of map-unique-sibling-keys is about the class that is not <unique>. If it refuses this, sibling keys do not join at all in a map literal with no type written: OpenVerse would refuse it.

A function with an any parameter, Ignore(X:any):int, named where a type{_(:int):int} is expected. (followup-variance/any-param asks a class below any with a function value; UEFN admits a function named at an any result, followup-refused/named-fn-any-result.) OpenVerse: refused, expected type{_(:int):int}, found type{_(:any):int}. If Epic refuses it (3502 or 3509), OpenVerse agrees on the verdict. If it admits it and prints value 7, a function named converts by contravariance from an any parameter: OpenVerse would convert it (an adapter that discards the argument).

A function with a <unique> class result, MakeToken():token, named where a function with a comparable result is expected, its two results compared. (followup-variance/comparable-result asks it of a function value.) OpenVerse: refused, expected type{_():comparable}, found type{_():token}. If Epic refuses it, OpenVerse agrees on the verdict. If it admits it and prints value different (two objects), a function named converts to a comparable result as it does to an any result: OpenVerse would convert it.

A rational compared with an int by <: 1 / 2 < 1. Compile only. Expected: refused by Epic (3509), which refused two rationals (differential/rat-ordering, a probe that also had an int). OpenVerse: refused, '<' does not order a rational (3509). If Epic refuses it (3509), OpenVerse agrees. If it admits it and prints less y, < takes a rational and an int though not two rationals: OpenVerse would admit that pair.

Two overloads on disjoint refinements of int (followup-refused/refinement-overloads, which UEFN admits and runs with literals), called with an int parameter that is no literal: F(N), N:int. OpenVerse: refused, no overload of F takes (int) (a call takes the overload its argument's type is of when compiled; an int is of neither without a cast). If Epic refuses it (3509), OpenVerse agrees. If it admits it and prints negative 0 small 1, the overload is chosen by the value when run: OpenVerse would dispatch on the value (and what an int in neither interval does would be the next question).

A spawned task with a child branch (whose defer prints) awaits an event, and a second task awaits the same event behind it. Signal resumes the first, which ends at once: is its branch's defer run before the second awaiter is resumed? OpenVerse: ran, runner resumed | branch cleanup | second awaiter | after signal | after wait (the task's children are stopped when its code ends, inside Signal, before the next awaiter runs). If Epic prints the same, OpenVerse agrees. If it prints runner resumed | second awaiter | branch cleanup | ..., or branch cleanup after after signal, a task's children are cancelled after the Signal's other awaiters have run (or at a later update): OpenVerse would defer that cancellation.

The same with the first awaiter a race arm that owns the branch: the arm is resumed by Signal and wins the race at once. Are its branch's defer, the losing arm's defer and the code after the race run before the second awaiter of the event is resumed? OpenVerse: ran, arm resumed | branch cleanup | loser cleanup | after race | second awaiter | after signal | after wait (the arm's task ends, its children and the loser are cancelled and the race's code goes on, all inside Signal before the next awaiter). If Epic prints the same, OpenVerse agrees. If second awaiter comes before branch cleanup, loser cleanup or after race, the event's other awaiters run before a finished race arm is cleaned up or before the race's task goes on: OpenVerse would order them so.

A spawn in a defer of a <suspends> function (UEFN admits and runs one in a function that does not suspend, followup-refused/spawn-in-defer): admitted, and when does the spawned task start and end? OpenVerse: refused, spawn in a defer of a <suspends> function is not supported (#156); a defer of a function that cannot suspend may spawn. If Epic refuses it, OpenVerse agrees on the verdict. If it admits it, its lines say what OpenVerse should do: run body done | side start | defer end | after run | side done | after wait is the spawned task started inside the defer, running to its first Sleep, and outliving the function.

cls-omitted-default-order with holder a struct: where does a struct's omitted default run among the values an archetype gives out of declaration order? OpenVerse: ran, value b | default c | value a | done 10 20 (as a class's). If Epic prints the same, OpenVerse agrees. Another order (value b | value a | default c, or default c first) would be a struct's rule, perhaps not a class's: OpenVerse would take it. If Epic refuses it, see struct-omitted-default-order-control (a struct may not hold or construct such a class).

Control for struct-omitted-default-order: does UEFN admit a struct with a field of a class type whose default constructs a class whose block prints (every field omitted)? OpenVerse: ran, default c | done 1 2. If Epic prints the same, struct-omitted-default-order asks only about order. If it refuses it, that probe's refusal says nothing about order.
